Uses expand quietly. A system approved for one purpose gets applied to others, and the expansion rarely comes back for a vote or a review.

For the readers near {{shortName}}, what is the current list of permitted uses, and how does it compare with the list at approval? Has anyone measured outcomes under any of them? An expanded purpose with no expanded measurement would mean less is known about the program now than when it started, and that direction of travel is what worries me.

It argues for stopping. What I would like is the {{readersWithinMile}} readers around campus removed and no new units approved in {{city}}. I am a student at {{school}}. Could you supply both versions of the permitted use list?

subject: Judging this by the standard you use elsewhere
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Every official has some initiative they consider wasteful, and the argument against it usually comes down to a lack of demonstrated results. I would ask you to turn that same lens on the plate readers around {{school}} and see how the program holds up.

No published objective, and no published outcome data. Nothing resembling an independent review either. By the standard applied to something already doubted, I do not think this would survive a first hearing.

Consistency seems to point one way. My own answer is the {{readersWithinMile}} readers near {{shortName}} removed and no new ones installed, or else the evidence produced that would let the program pass the test used on everything else. I am a student here. Which do you think is likelier?

subject: Comparing what the public heard with what was signed
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Two documents should say the same thing and often do not. Whatever residents were told when these cameras were proposed, and whatever the contract commits anyone to deliver, are worth reading side by side.

Could someone in your office do that comparison for the agreement covering {{shortName}}? Where the public promise includes outcomes while the contract includes only equipment and access, the promise was never enforceable and nobody was ever going to be held to it. That possibility concerns me.

Given it, I would like the {{readersWithinMile}} readers around campus removed and none installed to replace them. I am a student at {{school}}. What does the contract oblige the vendor to deliver, in terms anyone could measure?

subject: Counting installations is not measuring results
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Progress on this program tends to be described by how much equipment is deployed. Coverage expands, the count of installations rises, and the growth gets reported as though it were an achievement in itself.

Deployment is an input. There are {{readersInState}} of these devices across {{state}} now, which tells you about purchasing rather than about results. What has any of it produced?

I hope you will ask for outcome figures the next time expansion is described as progress. Meanwhile I would like the {{readersWithinMile}} readers around {{shortName}} removed and no new ones installed, since a count of hardware is the only figure this program has reliably published. I am a student at {{school}}. What outcome measure would you accept as an answer?

subject: Separating the cameras from a trend already moving
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Crime figures move for many reasons, most of which have nothing to do with any single program. Anyone crediting the readers near {{school}} with a change has to rule out the reasons already in motion, and that takes analysis rather than assertion.

Has anyone attempted it? A serious answer would name the method and show the comparison. Something less serious points at a chart with a line on it, and that is mostly what I have found.

Since the serious version has not appeared, I would ask you to support removing the {{readersWithinMile}} readers around {{shortName}} and approving no new installations. I am a student here. What analysis would you accept as ruling out the alternative explanations?

subject: What came back when your office asked for figures
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Assuming you have asked at some point, what came back? The response to a request for performance data is often more revealing than the data would be. A prompt answer with counts attached means the program is managed. Delay followed by generalities means it is not, and I would like to know which happened.

So I am asking about {{city}} and the readers near {{shortName}}, and I would be glad to see whatever you received.

Where nothing useful came back, the {{readersWithinMile}} readers around campus are running without accountability, and I would like them removed with no new ones approved. I am a student at {{school}}. What answer did you get, and when did it arrive?

subject: Making each new site wait for the last one
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Consider a rule that would change how these decisions get made. No new reader approved anywhere in {{city}} until the department publishes what the existing ones produced. Growth would then depend on results rather than on budget availability.

Applied to the area around {{shortName}}, that rule would freeze the program where it stands, which seems right to me, given that nothing has been published about the {{readersWithinMile}} devices already there.

What I would actually like goes further. I would like those readers taken down and none installed. Where that is out of reach, would you support the rule, and would you propose it at the next opportunity? I am a student at {{school}} and I would be grateful for either answer.

subject: Hoping the evidence arrives before the renewal vote
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

When this contract next comes to a vote, the question in front of you is narrow. Has anyone shown, with figures, that the plate readers near {{school}} did what they were bought to do?

Where the answer is no, continuing means spending on an unmeasured system, and it commits the next several years the way the last several were committed. That is what I would like to avoid.

So I am asking you to vote against renewal, to support taking down the {{readersWithinMile}} readers around {{shortName}}, and to approve no new installations. I am a student here, with one letter and no organization behind it. Should you plan to vote the other way, I would like to know what evidence you are relying on.

subject: The whole worry in a single question
body:
Dear {{officialName}},

Strip away everything else and one question remains. Does anybody know whether this program works, and if so, how? Every other argument about plate readers depends on the answer, and around {{shortName}} the answer appears to be that nobody knows and nobody has checked.

A public body operating equipment it cannot evaluate is what worries me. Either the evidence gets produced and published, in which case there is something real to argue about, or it does not, in which case I think the equipment should come down.

What I would like is the {{readersWithinMile}} readers near campus removed and no new ones installed. I am a student at {{school}}. Should you see it differently, please tell me what you know that I do not, and where it is written down.
